title: Checking How and Not What: A Test That Recorded the Calls Instead of Looking at the Motor

questions.question: A test records the calls made to a fake motor and compares them with a list. The program is changed to ramp in eight steps instead of four. What happens?
options: The test fails though the motor behaves as well or better, and the list is edited
questions.explanation: 5 of 5 harmless changes broke the test of the calls.

questions.question: What does a simulating fake keep that a recording fake does not?
options: The state of the motor, whether it is enabled and its speed, with the rules the real driver has
questions.explanation: It counts violations so a test can ask whether a rule was broken.

questions.question: A speed is set before the driver is enabled. What does the fake do?
options: Counts a violation and leaves the speed unchanged, as the hardware would ignore it
questions.explanation: A speed past the limit was counted and refused the same way.

questions.question: How many of the 5 harmless changes broke the state test, and how many of the 3 bugs did the state test catch?
Never enabling the driver is a bug both tests catch. What does only the state say?
options: That 4 speeds were ignored by the driver and the final speed is 0
questions.explanation: A failure that names the consequence can be acted on.

questions.question: When is a test of the call sequence the right one?
options: When the order is the requirement, such as a safety interlock that must disable before it moves, and it is chosen on purpose
questions.explanation: The lesson says to choose it deliberately and not by default.
